subject: Re: Azure private plan — audit access, SLA credits and execution path
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@mediq.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@mediq.com, Kunal Sharma <kunal.sharma@mediq.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private plan — audit access and SLA language

Irene,

Thanks for walking us through the Private Plan yesterday. Procurement had a quick review of the commercials and there are two items they want clarified before they raise a PO:  

1) Audit and evidence: they want narrow, scoped audit rights (on-sight or remote) limited to the annual SOC2 scope and for a prescriptive redaction process. Can you confirm Redwood's position on limited-scope audits and a 30-day notice window?

2) SLA credits and remediation: they want SLA credits tied to availability (monthly) and a commitment to a 60-day fix window for sev1/perf regressions that impact production integrations. The current Exhibit B doesn't specify remediation timing.

We can share our internal redlines if that helps — procurement would like to keep this moving this week.

Cheers,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior Procurement Manager, Mediq Health
procurement@mediq.com

--
Attachment: Mediq_Redlines_Request_20261029.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Azure private plan — audit access and SLA language

Team — forwarding Mediq procurement notes. Key asks: scoped audit (SOC2 scope, redaction), and explicit remediation timeline (they asked 60 days). Also they expect SLA credits monthly.

Can legal/commercial triage and propose language we can send back? If we agree to a limited-audit approach, suggest we require an approved security contact, a mutually-agreed statement of scope, and that Redwood provides artifacts first (SOC2 reports, penetration test summaries) prior to any remote/onsite audit.

Also note they asked to keep this moving this week — mark priority high.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Cloud Partnerships (Marketplace), Redwood Inference
--
Original message attached above

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Azure private plan — audit access and SLA language

Irene — looping legal and commercial notes below. Draft response and attached redlines (Exhibit B + SLA). Key points: 

- Audit: agree to limited remote audits scoped to SOC2 controls that are relevant to the service. We will require: (a) at least 30 days' written notice, (b) review of artifacts first (SOC2 report + pen test summary), (c) audits to be conducted off-hours where applicable, and (d) redaction of Mediq-sensitive customer IDs. No unfettered on-site access unless mutually agreed.

- SLA/remediation: we can accept a remediation target of 60 days for verified sev1 regressions caused by Redwood changes. We cannot commit to vendor-managed customer remediation (they must coordinate on integration fixes). We will add a service availability credit schedule (monthly credits capped at 100% of the monthly invoice for the impacted sku).

- Execution path: propose we prepare a single DocuSign bundle (Master Subscription + Exhibit B redlined + SOW) and request Mediq's PO trigger the DocuSign.

Attaching: Redwood-Azure_PrivatePlan_ExhibitB_redlined.pdf; Redwood-Azure_SLA_60day_remediation.docx

Next steps: 1) confirm internal acceptance of these bullets, 2) send to Mediq procurement with redlines + DocuSign link.

Marissa
Senior Commercial Counsel, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Redwood-Azure_PrivatePlan_ExhibitB_redlined.pdf (pdf stub)
Attachment: Redwood-Azure_SLA_60day_remediation.docx (docx stub)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@mediq.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@mediq.com, Kunal Sharma <kunal.sharma@mediq.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — audit access and SLA language

Irene/Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. Procurement reviewed and a few clarifying asks before we can sign: 

- The audit clause looks reasonable. Can you add a clause that any third-party auditors Mediq uses will be bound by mutual NDA language and limited to the stated SOC2 scope?

- For remediation: the 60-day target is acceptable, but Mediq needs an acknowledgement of interim mitigation responsibilities (we need a temporary rollback option or hotfix window). Can Redwood commit to a documented incident runbook and a named engineering escalation contact in the SOW?

- DocuSign: sending our PO is blocked until we receive the final DocuSign package. Please confirm when the final bundle will be uploaded; procurement prefers execution in the next three business days.

I attached a short procurement checklist for your commercial ops team.

Thanks,
Liam
--
Attachment: Mediq_Procurement_Checklist_20261103.pdf (pdf stub)
Link: https://www.docusign.com/Initiate?envelope=0a1b2c3d

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@mediq.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — audit access and SLA language

Liam — appreciate the checklist and clear asks. Finalizing on our side:  

1) Auditor NDA: agreed. We'll add a clause that any Mediq-selected third-party auditor must sign Redwood's standard auditor NDA and be limited to SOC2 controls relevant to the service.

2) Interim mitigation/runbook: we will include a short incident runbook appendix and name a 24/7 engineering escalation contact for the first 90 days post-activation. We'll also commit to a documented hotfix/rollback path for production-impacting releases.

3) DocuSign bundle: commercial ops will upload the final envelope today. Expect: Master Subscription Agreement (redlined), Exhibit B (redlined), and SOW with named contacts. We'll email the DocuSign link once it's live — ETA today (5 Nov).

If that timeline works, please confirm and procurement can route the PO on receipt of the envelope. Happy to hop on a five-minute call if you want to confirm any technical points.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

--
